name: PrOP-M
def: Small tethered walking rover carried by the Mars 2 and Mars 3 landers, intended to skid across the surface on twin skis.
body: Each PrOP-M was a squat box that moved on two powered skis rather than wheels, connected to its lander by a 15 metre umbilical and steered by simple contact logic that reversed and turned at obstacles. A manipulator arm was to lift the rover onto the ground, after which it would leave tracks and take penetrometer and radiation density readings within view of the lander cameras. Mars 2 crashed in November 1971 and Mars 3 stopped transmitting seconds after landing, so neither rover was ever deployed.
facts: First rovers sent to Mars, neither of which operated
Tether limited operation to 15 metres from the lander
specs: Two powered skis with obstacle contact reversing
Supplied by cable from the lander
Hardwired reflex behaviour on contact with obstacles
